title: Deterministic estimator cost
statement: Given a small-bias Fourier input and a finite set $U$ of output coordinates, the deterministic Fourier estimator cost is the sum of the cost of the deterministic generator's local work and the Fourier estimator's cost on $U$ using the prescribed sample count. Its random-example and query counts are zero, apart from any contributions in the estimator cost.
hypotheses_covered: The underlying bias input has output dimension $n>0$.
Twice the bias numerator is at most the bias denominator.
The Fourier bound is a natural number at least one.
$U$ is a finite set of output coordinates.
caveat: The supplied statement does not define either component cost, so their detailed dependence on the parameters cannot be rendered.
